decisions.context: The mockup requires a persistent asset/layout palette, safe editable canvas, properties sidebar, and layers tree with pointer/touch dragging, while the repository requires an equivalent keyboard path, canonical slot operations, React 19 desktop/thin parity, bounded behavior, and production packaging.

consequences: Package and lock files change and dependency security/build/package gates become mandatory
A thin shared interaction adapter maps palette insert, within-slot reorder, cross-slot reparent, and layout operations onto pure draft/application commands
The four-region editor shell, responsive drawers, properties tabs, and Layers and Structure tree remain repository-owned shared UI
No drag library type or event crosses into contracts, application, persistence, transports, or immutable revisions
options.label: dnd-kit canonical adapter
options.summary: Use the mature @dnd-kit/core and @dnd-kit/sortable packages only as a shared pointer/touch/keyboard interaction adapter; translate every accepted drop into existing canonical draft commands, with custom slot collision rules, drag handles, overlays, instructions, announcements, and unchanged native action controls.
tradeoffs: Adds pinned audited UI dependencies and a modest client bundle cost
Provides maintained pointer, touch, keyboard, overlay, sensor, and sortable foundations
Still requires repository-specific collision, compatibility, focus restoration, announcements, and exhaustive nested-slot tests
Keeps the visual shell declarative and preserves one command/state model across all input methods

consequences: Package and lock files change and dependency security/build/package gates become mandatory
The editor must provide explicit move menus or buttons as the authoritative keyboard alternative
Shared UI owns live-region messaging, focus restoration, and all semantic tree behavior
options.label: Pragmatic DnD adapter
options.summary: Use Atlassian Pragmatic Drag and Drop for pointer direct manipulation and keep keyboard movement in the existing explicit action/menu path with custom live announcements.
tradeoffs: Smaller framework coupling and strong performance-oriented primitives
Accessibility behavior is intentionally separate from the core package and must be assembled in this repository
Pointer and keyboard paths use different interaction mechanisms even though they converge on the same commands
Nested named-slot collision and drag-preview behavior still require substantial custom code

consequences: The roadmap grows materially and direct-manipulation qualification becomes a larger independent risk boundary
Repository code must own every sensor and accessibility behavior for both Electron and supported browsers
No package changes are needed, but substantially more shared UI infrastructure and maintenance are introduced
options.label: Repository-owned pointer engine
options.summary: Implement direct manipulation with Pointer Events, geometry measurement, custom overlays, auto-scroll, collision detection, touch activation, keyboard pickup/move/drop, and live announcements without a third-party drag dependency.
tradeoffs: Avoids a production dependency and gives complete behavior control
Largest implementation, accessibility, browser-compatibility, performance, and maintenance burden
High risk of duplicating mature sensor, cancellation, scrolling, overlay, and focus behavior
Requires broader test fixtures across mouse, touch, pen, keyboard, zoom, and nested scroll containers

decisions.question: Which interaction engine should power direct manipulation in the shared visual System Composer?
decisions.title: Visual composer drag interaction

constraints: Use the existing canonical SystemBuilderRevision, AssetComposition, AssetInstance, AssetPlacement, AssetBinding, exact definitions, and application validators; drag state is transient UI state only.
The visual canvas must represent predefined named slots and semantic ordering rather than arbitrary coordinates, user-authored dimensions, or renderer-only layout metadata.
Every pointer or touch drop must resolve to the same pure bounded add, reorder, reparent, wrap, or layout-remap operation used by the complete keyboard and button path.

The center canvas may render only registered side-effect-free Foundation surfaces and safe fixtures; it must never execute unqualified backing resources, imported code, backend logic, or deployment behavior.
Desktop and thin client must consume one shared editor shell and one platform client contract with exact workspace context, optimistic save conflicts, and no host-specific composition policy.
The wide mockup layout should keep palette, canvas, properties, and layers visible; narrower layouts must use accessible drawers or panel tabs without losing function, focus order, or source order.
Selection, focus, hover, drag overlay, zoom, panel size, and open-panel state are presentation state and must not enter immutable system revisions.
A layout change for an existing system must be explicit, previewable, cancelable, and deterministic, preserving compatible content and exposing unmatched content rather than silently deleting it.
Any new drag-and-drop dependency must be version-pinned, license/security reviewed, isolated behind shared UI interaction adapters, and verified in desktop packaging and thin-client builds.
Keep the old slot-composer roadmap stopped after its verified Increment 3; do not resume its unstarted Increment 4 in parallel with this replacement roadmap.

discovery.summary: The completed slot-composer foundations already provide exact workspace asset discovery, required system roots, predefined application/page layouts, canonical named slots and placements, pure add/reorder/reparent/wrap/remove draft operations, protected nodes, bounded undo/redo, schema-generated configuration, typed connections, a keyboard tree, safe recursive preview, and desktop/thin-client parity. The current UI does not yet match the supplied visual-composer mockup: creation controls and layout choices sit above the editor, the asset/canvas/tree workspace exists only in Structure mode, configuration and connections replace the whole workspace, the center is a semantic hierarchy rather than a safe editable visual rendering, and no pointer/touch drag interaction exists. The mockup can therefore be implemented as a shared interaction and presentation layer over the existing canonical draft, with one application-owned layout-remapping seam where changing an existing layout requires deterministic placement mapping. No new persistence graph or renderer-owned system truth is needed.

name: Visual System Composer
objective: Deliver a production-ready visual System Composer that builds on canonical named slots and placements with a mockup-aligned asset and layout palette, safe editable canvas, synchronized properties and layers panels, accessible drag-and-drop, and shared desktop/thin-client behavior.
